workarounds.symptom: GoogleMatchingEngine logs the full service account private key at DEBUG
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(vector-store): stop writing service account private key to DEBUG logs in GoogleMatchingEngine. Target files: mem0/vector_stores/vertex_ai_vector_search.py, tests/vector_stores/test_vertex_ai_vector_search.py. `GoogleMatchingEngine.__init__` logged the whole `kwargs` dict and the validated config dump at DEBUG. With `service_account_json` passed inline that wrote the PEM private key verbatim to the log sink — the field mem0's own `_SENSITIVE_FIELDS_EXACT` classifies as a secret. (Ref: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/pull/7506)

workarounds.symptom: add() mutates the caller's filters object, leaking scope into the next add() and bypassing the required-scope check
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(ts-oss): stop add() from mutating the caller's filters object. Target files: mem0-ts/src/oss/src/memory/index.ts, mem0-ts/src/oss/tests/memory.add-filters-isolation.test.ts. `add()` destructured `filters` by reference and wrote the resolved scope into it: (Ref: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/pull/6797)

workarounds.symptom: Relax version constraints in `peerDependencies` to avoid conflicts
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(ts-sdk): stop forcing pg on installs (optional ranged pg peer, optional natural). Target files: mem0-ts/package.json, mem0-ts/src/oss/src/vector_stores/pgvector.ts, mem0-ts/pnpm-lock.yaml. `mem0ai` forced `pg` onto every install in two ways. npm 7+ and pnpm auto-install required peers, so both applied even to hosted `MemoryClient` users: (Ref: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/pull/7450)

workarounds.symptom: Python SDK: documented dev setup fails — ruff/isort/pre-commit not installed in hatch dev environments
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: wire dev tooling (ruff/isort/pre-commit) into hatch dev environments. Target files: pyproject.toml. Following CONTRIBUTING.md's documented Python SDK setup exactly — `hatch shell dev_py_3_11` → `pre-commit install` → `make lint` / `make format` / `make sort` — fails on a fresh clone: - `pre-commit install` → `pre-commit: command not found` - `make lint` / `make format` → `ruff: command not found` - `make sort` → `isort: command not found` Root cause: `ruff`, `isort`, and `pytest` are declared in the `dev` optional- dependen... (Ref: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/pull/6684)

workarounds.symptom: bug(llms/aws_bedrock): Anthropic Converse parsing crashes when a reasoningContent block precedes the text block
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(llms/aws_bedrock): iterate Converse content blocks for Anthropic text. Target files: mem0/llms/aws_bedrock.py, tests/llms/test_aws_bedrock.py. The Anthropic branch of `_generate_standard` parsed the Converse API response with `content[0]`, which assumes the first content block is the text block. Reasoning-enabled Claude models emit a `reasoningContent` block first (KeyError), and some stop conditions produce an empty content array (IndexError); both surface as an unhelpful generic `RuntimeError` from `generate_response`.
